title: Go: Worker Pool Pattern
description: Implement the classic worker pool pattern using goroutines and channels for task distribution.

steps.title: Create jobs channel
steps.description: Create a buffered channel `jobs chan int` with capacity 10. Send 5 job IDs (1-5) and close the channel. Print each job after sending using `fmt.Printf("Sent job %d\n", job)`.
hints: Use `make(chan int, 10)` for the jobs channel
Send each job ID with `jobs <- id`
Close the channel after sending all jobs with `close(jobs)`

verification.failureMessage: Make sure to close the jobs channel after sending all jobs.

steps.title: Worker function
steps.description: Write a `worker(id int, jobs <-chan int, results chan<- int)` function that receives jobs from a channel, simulates work with sleep, and sends the job*2 as a result. Print "Worker X started job Y" and "Worker X finished job Y".
hints: Use `for j := range jobs` to keep reading until jobs channel is closed
The worker takes a receive-only jobs channel and send-only results channel
Print before and after processing each job

verification.successMessage: Worker processes jobs from the channel!
verification.failureMessage: The worker should loop over jobs with range until closed.

steps.title: Distribute work
steps.description: Launch 3 workers. Send 10 jobs (values 1-10) to the jobs channel. Each worker picks up jobs concurrently. Print "Job X processed by worker Y".
hints: Launch workers as goroutines before sending jobs
Use `go worker(i, jobs, results)` to start each worker
Workers automatically pick up jobs as they become available

verification.successMessage: Workers distributed the jobs among themselves!
verification.failureMessage: Launch multiple workers as goroutines before sending jobs.

steps.title: Collect results
steps.description: Collect all 10 results from the results channel. Print each result using `fmt.Printf("Result: %d\n", result)`. The results channel is buffered with capacity 10.
hints: Create `results := make(chan int, 10)` for collecting output
Receive from results channel in a loop: `for i := 0; i < 10; i++`
Results may arrive in any order

verification.successMessage: All results collected from the worker pool!
verification.failureMessage: Make sure you receive results for each job sent.

steps.title: Graceful shutdown
steps.description: Add a `done` channel to signal workers to stop early. After sending 3 of 10 jobs, send a stop signal. Workers check a `done` channel via select and exit early. Print "Worker Y shutting down".
hints: Use a `done := make(chan struct{})` as a stop signal
Inside worker, use `select { case j, ok := <-jobs: ...; case <-done: ... }`
Close or send on the done channel to trigger shutdown

verification.failureMessage: Use select to listen for both jobs and done channels.
